summary: Not as a dip-buying signal. On BTC, ETH and SOL, price after RSI went below 30, or crossed back up through 30, moved the same as after random candles on 1h, 4h and daily. The result that holds up runs the other way: after RSI(14) went above 70, price kept rising, so shorts opened there did worse than random, and that gap comes from uptrends.

verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily, with RSI(7) or RSI(14).
Same as random on 4h and daily with both lengths. On 1h, RSI(14) looked worse than random only because of signals on Nov 7–9, 2022.
Worse than random on 1h, 4h and daily, because price kept rising after RSI(14) went above 70. The gap comes from uptrends. Below the 200-day SMA it was same as random on 1h and 4h.
Same as random on 1h and daily. On 4h it looked worse than random only because of SOL's signals between Jan 31, 2021 and Feb 11, 2021.
Same as random on 1h and 4h. On daily it beat random only because of the stretch between Dec 29, 2020 and Jul 7, 2021. Without that stretch it was same as random.

notes: Buying while RSI(14) was below 30 on 4h gave 1,864 entries in 302 separate moves. Twenty candles later they trailed random entries by 0.31%, inside the luck band. RSI(7), Gainium's default length, enters about two and a half times as often. It also landed inside the band.

Shorting while RSI(14) was above 70 did 0.36% worse than random after 20 candles on 1h. It did 1.26% worse on 4h and 10% worse after 20 days on daily. On 1h and 4h the gap shows at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles and holds without its strongest stretch. On daily it holds without its strongest stretch but is back inside the band at 50 and 100 candles.

Uptrends carry that result. On 4h, a short above 70 did 1.2% worse than random while the pair closed above its 200-day SMA. Below it, the short did 0.7% worse, which is inside the luck band. On 1h the split is the same: 0.44% worse in uptrends, same as random in downtrends. On daily, downtrends gave too few separate moves to judge.

Going long while RSI(14) was above 50 beat random by 2.92% after 20 days on daily. The gap rests on the stretch between Dec 29, 2020 and Jul 7, 2021, and at 50 and 100 candles it is gone. On daily in downtrends, and on 1h and 4h overall, it was same as random.

Single stretches can fake a result. On 1h, RSI(14) crossing up through 30 looked worse than random only because of signals on Nov 7–9, 2022, during the FTX collapse, when bounces failed. On 4h, RSI(7) below 30 in downtrends looked worse for the same reason, with its strongest stretch on Nov 6–14, 2022. On 4h, the short on a cross down through 70 looked bad only because of SOL's signals between Jan 31, 2021 and Feb 11, 2021.

For a long DCA bot on these pairs, an RSI-below-30 start condition timed entries no better than a random candle. The DCA orders and take profit decide the outcome there. RSI(14) above 70 is where price showed a shape: it tended to keep rising, mostly above the 200-day SMA. That is a reason to leave an overbought start out of a short bot in an uptrend. A long bot can also use the reading as a trend filter beside its own conditions.
